Prototype

The Progress page

Analytics, sprints, goals and threads, all in one place. It isn’t built yet, which is the whole point of showing you now: it’s far cheaper to change a web page than a shipped feature.

It really works, up to a point. Add a thread and settle it. Set a goal from a preset. Start a sprint and watch the clock run. The figures come from the same Sherlock Holmes book Penpoint gives you when you click Demo, so the names should already look familiar. Nothing you do is saved anywhere; refresh and it’s all back.

What I’d like you to check

  • The Dashboard — is the right thing the biggest thing on it?
  • Sprints — start one from the Dashboard. The countdown keeps running if you switch tabs, on purpose.
  • Goals — try a preset. Do the worldbuilding ones make sense as goals?
  • Threads — the loose ends in your book (the continuity slip, the name you haven’t settled). Note one, open it, and point its body at a character or a chapter with an @. Does “thread” land, or would you rather it said to-do?
  • The sentence under today’s word count — it changes each time you come back to the Dashboard. Too clever, or the best part?

Use the strip at the bottom to change theme, text size, or to see the page on a brand-new book with no history behind it.

Thanks! — Joel
